questions.q: A candidate paper has no released code and no checkpoints. According to the three filters in this lesson, what should you do?
options: Proceed anyway and reimplement the method from the paper's prose
Reject it as a capstone candidate and look for a paper that releases code and checkpoints
Email the authors and wait for a reply before deciding
Pick it only if the paper is very recent
questions.explain: Released code and checkpoints is the first filter. Without them you're forced into reimplementing from prose first and comparing to the reported number second, which Lesson 7 already identified as backwards.

questions.q: Why does this lesson favor a paper with one clear headline number over a paper with a sprawling table of many results?
options: A single number is easier to put on a slide
A single, unambiguous claim gives you a crisp definition of done for the reproduction
Papers with many results are always fake
Headline numbers are always higher than secondary results
questions.explain: A single headline number lets you say clearly whether you landed near it or not, which is exactly the crisp target a capstone timeline needs.

questions.q: Which of these is an example used in this lesson of a result that fits all three selection filters?
options: Pretraining a frontier-scale LLM from scratch
A small ResNet trained on CIFAR-10
A multi-hundred-GPU multi-week training run
A result with no public code or benchmark number
questions.explain: A small ResNet on CIFAR-10 has released reference code, runs on modest single-GPU compute, and reduces to one clean, well-known error number.

questions.q: What is the purpose of writing a capstone PROPOSAL.md before writing any training code?
options: It is required by paperswithcode.com before you may reproduce a result
It fixes the paper, target number, compute budget, and timeline so the scope is decided before coding begins
It replaces the need for a README
It is only useful after the extension phase is finished
questions.explain: The proposal exists to lock in scope — paper, target number, compute, and a rough reproduction-versus-extension timeline — before any code gets written.

questions.q: In the suggested capstone repo skeleton, what should the first script under scripts/ do?
options: Immediately launch your own reimplementation of the method
Run the official authors' code using its own baseline command, before you change anything
Deploy the model to a production endpoint
Generate the final write-up report
questions.explain: Consistent with Lesson 7's playbook, the first thing the repo should run is the official code's own command, so you confirm it works before introducing any of your own changes.
